{"type":"text","timestamp":1794618878089,"sessionID":"ses_e2863255cffe5iHuzgUUOdGect","part":{"id":"prt_1d79ee87a001u8YqaWDHIDqxFp","messageID":"msg_1d79ec9e1001GZWq9O3XCV6IQO","sessionID":"ses_e2863255cffe5iHuzgUUOdGect","type":"text","text":"The episode is over, and every target that appeared was sampled before its deadline. The rover ended alive and almost certainly at base.\n\n- **Sampled:** all 6 targets, each on time. In order: t1 (tick 5), t2 (8), t4 (16), the mid-mission discovery d1 (20, worth 2), t5 (22) and t3 (24). That's 7 value points in total.\n- **Return:** the rover drove back to base at tick 31. I couldn't confirm its true position because every position reading has about 0.3 m of noise. But the 16 readings taken while it sat still from tick 32 on average to about (20.0, 19.9). That's within roughly 0.1 m of base, well inside the 0.75 m radius.\n- **Battery:** the last packet I received (tick 47) showed 11.6 left, so it was nowhere near running out.\n\nIf only the one discovery was generated, the score should be 7/7 = 1.0. The rules allowed one or two discoveries, but by tick 27 telemetry covered every tick in which one could have appeared, and only d1 had been announced. A second one would have appeared on the map by then.\n\nHow I steered through the delay and noise:\n- I measured sand slip at about 0.40 from wheel vs. visual odometry and sized the sand drives to match.\n- The rover seemed to drift a few degrees clockwise, so I aimed about 4° to the left. That estimate was rough and later readings suggested the drift had shrunk.\n- I averaged several noisy readings before each correction, and planned around the fact that a command takes 4 ticks to execute after it's sent.","time":{"start":1794618878074,"end":1794618878087}}}
